title: Admin Snaglet: proactive prober that converts detected support signals into safe runbook tasks
creator: Ayesha Rao
description:
Problem: On-call engineers spend significant time triaging recurring low-variety incidents that follow a predictable remediation path. Current runbooks exist as docs and occasionally as manual task templates; we lack a lightweight, auditable bridge that can detect a signal, create a safe, permissioned runbook task, and optionally execute idempotent remediation steps in a controlled manner.

Proposal: Build "Admin Snaglet", a small probe-and-task system that: (1) runs configurable probes (metrics, log patterns, synthetic checks), (2) converts positive probes into a runbook-as-task (typed inputs, allowed actions), (3) attaches a safety harness (dry-run, permission gate, TTL, approval requirement), and (4) integrates with our admin microtask runner to allow one-click or automated remediation. The goal is to reduce time-to-first-action for common incidents while preserving auditability and operator control.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Snaglet can be provisioned per-namespace with a JSON probe spec and a runbook template reference.
2) When a probe fires, a linear task is created with typed params and a link to a generated ephemeral sandbox for dry-run.
3) Tasks include clear safety metadata: required RBAC role, dry-run flag, TTL, and a revert playbook if remediation runs.
4) In a gated rollout, the system must not auto-execute without explicit approval unless tenant opt-in flag is set.
5) Telemetry emits probe -> task -> action traces with timing and operator identity.
6) End-to-end tests demonstrate at least 3 sample runbooks (cache-eviction, model-serving-kv-cache-warm, routing-fallback).
implementation_notes:
Architecture: lightweight controller in ops-service that subscribes to probe results (Prometheus alerts, log router hooks, synthetic heartbeat). Probes are authored as small YAML/JSON with selectors, threshold windows, and severity. When a probe becomes active the controller builds a typed runbook task payload using the runbook template API. Safety: actions are parameterized and executed via the existing admin microgateway which enforces an allowlist, idempotency checks, and a sandboxed dry-run channel.

Key design choices considered:
- Where to keep probe definitions: chose per-namespace store in vault-backed config to enable per-tenant tuning.
- Auto-exec vs manual: default to manual with an explicit opt-in flag per-probe.
- Task representation: reuse Linear-style task metadata we already have plus additional 'safety' fields so dashboards can filter.

Implementation tasks:
- Controller: subscribe to event bus + probe evaluator (Marcus)
- Runbook template adapter: translate templates to task inputs (Ayesha)
- Safety gate: hook into RBAC microservice (security review)
- UI: quick 'triage' panel in ops console to review Snaglet-created tasks (PM/UX TBD)
- E2E tests and chaos scenarios (SRE)

Security notes: secrets used by probes (e.g., metric write keys) must be pulled from KMS and never stored in cleartext. All actions executed must be logged to audit and tied to operator identity.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (internal alpha): single team namespace, probe types: Prometheus threshold + log regex. No auto-exec. Collect telemetry and human feedback (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (expanded beta): add synthetic probes and two more namespaces, enable optional scheduled auto-exec behind tenant opt-in flag and additional approval workflow.
Phase 3 (GA): integrations with admin microgateway full action set, console UI for probe authoring, and defaults for common runbooks.

Canary plan: start with non-critical remediations (cache clear, metadata refresh). Use feature flag and audit every triggered task for 72h. Revert plan: disable probes via feature flag and revoke opt-in tokens.
telemetry_kpis:
- Mean time from probe-firing to task-creation (target < 15s)
- Percentage of snaglet tasks that progress to operator review within 30m (target > 75%)
- Reduction in median time-to-first-action for targeted incident classes (target 30% improvement)
- Number of auto-executions blocked by safety gate (monitor for false positives)
- Audit log completeness (100%)
